# ZViewer

> ZViewer is an offline native Android comic reader for local archives (ZIP/CBZ, RAR/CBR, 7Z), PDF, image folders, and video folders, built with Kotlin 2.1.21 and Jetpack Compose (Material 3).

Package `dev.zolive.zviewer`, MIT license. The latest stable release is [1.8.5](https://github.com/Zo-Live/ZViewer/releases/tag/v1.8.5) (`versionCode 28`). The app supports Android 10 and later (minSdk 29, compile and target SDK 36). The universal APK covers `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64`. Reading runs on-device through a persisted Storage Access Framework (SAF) grant. The interface defaults to Simplified Chinese and also supports Traditional Chinese, English, and Japanese.

## Features

- The library scans folders recursively and offers covers, search, natural filename sorting (`2.jpg` before `10.jpg`), and horizontally scrollable reading-status filters. Swipe between Library, Favorites, and Recently Read. Each tab keeps its scroll position and shows a return-to-top button after scrolling. Long-press a cover to enter favorite management, where tapping a cover or its button toggles the favorite. Search, filters, sorting, and tab switches keep management mode on. The close button, Settings, refresh, system back, or picking a new library folder exits it.
- Reader: continuous vertical scrolling or horizontal paging, optional right-to-left paging, loop mode (first and last pages adjoin), pinch / double-tap / button zoom from 1× to 5×, page jump, keep screen on, and saved per-page and per-video progress.
- Video: folders or archives that contain only videos, or a mix of images and videos, open in one pager that follows the vertical/horizontal setting. The seek slider appears only on video pages. Options: loop a single video, or open in preview mode (paused until tapped). Codec support depends on the device's Media3 / system decoders.
- Settings includes Appearance (theme and accent color), Preferences (language, 2–5 cover columns, file type labels off by default, and favorite icons on by default), Reading (reading mode, dark reader background, right-to-left paging, keep screen on, single-video loop, video preview, and loop mode), Library & Storage, Diagnostics, and App (check for updates, startup checks off by default, About, and a GitHub repository link). The link opens in GitHub Mobile when available and otherwise uses Android's link handler. Swipe right or use system back to return from settings or the log screens.
- Library & Storage lets you choose the library folder, see cache size, set a cache limit, and double-tap to clear the reading cache or reading history. Manual cache clearing includes covers and video frames when Clear covers is enabled. Separate switches can clear the cache or reading history when the app is removed from Android Recents. Keep only current library cache removes other libraries' cached reading files, covers, and video frames after a successful scan of the selected library. Generate missing covers can process the whole library from Settings, during reading, or while the app is in the background and the process is alive. These switches are off by default.
- Optional diagnostics write to the app-specific `logs/` directory or a SAF folder the user picks. Settings can show, copy, share, export, and clear existing logs, including after logging is turned off. The list includes the default directory and historical log directories with a persisted read/write grant.
- Extracted pages, copied images, fallback copies of non-seekable PDFs, and temporary cover sources live in the app cache. Complete covers and video frames persist under app files. Their combined size is compared with a configurable limit (256 MiB–8 GiB, default 1.5 GiB). At the limit, idle reading files and incomplete temporary files are trimmed to about two-thirds of the limit. Open books and files still being written are protected. Complete covers and frames are exempt from size-based trimming, so the limit is soft. Cache and reading history cleanup preserve original files and favorites.

## Supported Formats

| Kind | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Archives | `zip`, `cbz`, `rar`, `cbr`, `7z` (via libarchive) |
| Documents | `pdf` (via `PdfRenderer`; library root or plain subfolders only) |
| Static images | `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `bmp`, `heif`, `heic`, `avif` |
| Animated images | `apng`, animated `webp`, `gif`, animated `avif` |
| Video | `mp4`, `m4v`, `mkv`, `webm`, `avi`, `mov`, `3gp`, `3g2`, `mpg`, `mpeg`, `mpe`, `ts`, `mts`, `m2ts`, `mpegts`, `flv`, `wmv`, `ogv`, `vob`, `rm`, `rmvb` |

Not supported: encrypted or multi-volume archives, password-protected PDFs, PDFs inside archives (the user is asked to extract them first), DRM content, animated HEIF. HEIF/HEIC decoding depends on the device. A solid 7Z archive has to be fully prepared on first open.

## Architecture

Source root: `app/src/main/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/`.

- `MainActivity.kt`: the single Activity; edge-to-edge Compose host.
- `LibraryViewModel.kt`: app state, SAF folder selection, scan/open jobs, error mapping, settings, and progress.
- `data/Models.kt`: `Book`, `BookSession`, media-aware `PageSource`, `ReadingProgress`, `ReaderSettings`, `ReaderException`.
- `data/NaturalOrder.kt`: natural numbers, Latin letters, phrase-aware Chinese pinyin and Japanese collation for names containing kana. The library, pages and covers use the same ordering.
- `data/UpdateChecker.kt`, `data/UpdateDownloader.kt`, and `ui/UpdateFeedback.kt` check stable GitHub releases with persistent caching for newer releases (60 seconds for manual checks and 6 hours at startup), ETag revalidation, bounded timeouts, and numeric version comparison. Failed or up-to-date checks can be retried immediately. Android DownloadManager handles background downloads. The app checks the APK's package and version and opens the system installer when a non-reading screen is active and the app has resumed. Short feedback uses Android system Toasts, and new releases use a confirmation dialog. Startup checks only announce new releases.
- `data/PreferenceStore.kt`: SharedPreferences storage for the tree URI, the book index JSON, reading progress, favorites, settings, and log options. Image and video positions use a media key derived from the SAF URI or archive member name. A stored page number is used when its media key is missing. Video positions from older builds are migrated by page index when the page count still matches.
- `data/BookRepository.kt`: bulk `DocumentsContract` queries, background extraction, PDF sources, video preparation, cover and page caches, and safety limits.
- `data/PdfDocument.kt` and `ui/PdfReaderPages.kt` reuse one renderer per reading session. Seekable SAF files open directly, with a local cache copy as the fallback for non-seekable sources. PDF pages are rendered into memory, prioritizing visible pages and then one page on each side in either reading mode.
- `data/CacheLimits.kt`: cache-limit bounds and normalization (256 MiB–8 GiB, 256 MiB steps, 1.5 GiB default).
- `data/ReadingCache.kt` accounts for reading files and persistent covers and frames, reconciles caches after a successful scan, trims idle reading files and incomplete files in LRU order, and migrates legacy covers. Repositories accessing the same cache share reference counts. Capacity scans run outside the reference lock. Cleanup after removal from Android Recents defers deletion of in-use files until the final reference is released.
- `data/DiagnosticLog.kt` and `ui/LogScreen.kt` record and manage local diagnostics. Logs cover device/display/resources, permissions/settings, lifecycle, scan/open timings, reading/cache/update activity, media failures, and uncaught exceptions. Lines include timestamp, level, category, process, thread, and uptime. A 512-entry queue serializes writes on an I/O dispatcher. Each file is capped at about 2 MiB (crashes may exceed this), and the default folder keeps up to five sessions. An unwritable SAF directory falls back to the default directory. URIs are redacted; routine events use shortened book IDs. Exception stacks may contain paths.
- `reader/ImageLoader.kt`: APNG detection from PNG chunks, AVIF via APNG4Android + libavif, all other formats via `ImageDecoder`.
- `reader/SampledAnimationDrawable.kt`: draws animations at a downsampled target size.
- `reader/ZoomImageView.kt`, `reader/ZoomVideoView.kt`: native matrix zoom/pan inside an `AndroidView`. Unzoomed gestures pass through to the Compose list or pager. The video view keeps a cached first-frame cover behind the Media3 `TextureView`.
- `reader/ReaderPaging.kt`: maps virtual loop positions to real page numbers for `LazyColumn` / `HorizontalPager`.
- `ui/LibraryScreen.kt`: `ZViewerApp` entry point, library tabs and grid, search/filter, continue-reading card, favorite management.
- `ui/ReaderScreen.kt` hosts image pages, PDF pages, the video pager, and the shared reader toolbar.
- `ui/VideoReader.kt`: Media3 playback. Details are below.
- `ui/SettingsScreen.kt`, `ui/Theme.kt`: Material 3 settings (with the swipe-right exit gesture) and theming.

Video playback design (`ui/VideoReader.kt`):

- The player pool preloads videos for the settled page and its two neighbours, at most three players. Each off-screen neighbour can render its saved-position frame into its own `TextureView` before a swipe. A player is released once its page is two or more positions away or leaves the composition, so aborted or back-and-forth drags within that range reuse the same instance. Only those three virtual items get players, even when loop mode repeats a real page. Pages farther out display a cover from a bounded session cache that evicts the oldest inserted cover.
- No flashing: every video page has the same `AndroidView` structure with or without a player. The Media3 shutter is transparent and the cover sits behind the video until the first frame paints over it. Each player belongs to exactly one view, and ownership moves by detaching the old view before binding the new one. Playback also requires the owning surface to be attached.
- `repeatMode` is set only from the loop settings and is never changed during transitions. Changing it near the end of a clip makes ExoPlayer reinitialize its output and flash. Instead, a video that ends mid-transition restarts from the beginning in `onEnded`, and a finished video restarts when the user returns to it.
- Video folders play directly from SAF URIs. Videos inside archives play from extracted files. Covers for video books come from `MediaMetadataRetriever`; mixed folders/archives use the first media item in natural order (an image or a video frame).

After the user picks a folder, the app persists the SAF read grant, scans the folder in the background, and saves the book index. It generates covers on demand or in the background when Generate missing covers is enabled. In the reader it decodes images, renders PDFs, or plays videos, extracting archive media to cache as needed. The app saves the current page and per-video playback positions.

## Privacy and Security

- The app uses `INTERNET` for GitHub update checks and APK downloads. The repository link opens in another app. There are no accounts, ads, telemetry, or external-storage permissions. Reading files stay on the device, and diagnostic logs leave it only through a user-initiated share or export.
- Reading files are accessed within the granted library directory. Original files are preserved.
- Backup and device-to-device transfer are disabled, so URI grants don't move with app data.
- Archive members are written under generated sequential filenames. Hidden files, `__MACOSX`, symlinks, and unsupported entries are skipped. Member names are decoded as UTF-8 (`Archive.setCharset`) so Chinese names work.
- Limits include 20,000 extracted image or video entries per archive, 256 MiB per extracted or copied image, 4 GiB per extracted or copied video, 4 GiB total extracted per archive, 4 GiB per local PDF copy, and a library directory scan depth of 32.

## Build and Test

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK 36, the bundled Gradle 8.11.1 wrapper (AGP 8.10.1), and network access to download dependencies.

```sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android"
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug
python3 tools/generate_fixtures.py
./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest   # instrumented tests on an emulator/device
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease             # signed release build
```

- Unit tests in `app/src/test/` cover version parsing and comparison (`AppVersionTest`), filename ordering and media recognition (`NaturalOrderTest`), cache limits, migration, and reconciliation (`ReadingCacheTest`), and reader paging (`ReaderPagingTest`).
- Instrumented tests in `app/src/androidTest/` cover formats, video playback, paging and reader gestures, navigation and favorites, language menus, cache settings and cleanup, seekable and non-seekable PDFs, diagnostics, and update checks and downloads. `FixtureDocumentsProvider` provides SAF access to test files.
- Run `python3 tools/generate_fixtures.py` before running the instrumented tests on a clean checkout. It also invokes the video generator and writes to `tools/fixtures/`, which is packaged as androidTest assets. Dependencies and executable paths are listed in the architecture documentation.
- Emulator UI smoke scripts (uiautomator2): `tools/ui_smoke.py`, `tools/ui_navigation_smoke.py`, `tools/ui_cache_smoke.py`, `tools/ui_update_smoke.py`. `tools/collect_licenses.py` regenerates the open source notices.
- Release signing: `.signing/zviewer-release.jks` (alias `zviewer`), with passwords from `ZVIEWER_STORE_PASSWORD` / `ZVIEWER_KEY_PASSWORD`. Never commit `.signing/`.
- Development Release builds go to `app/build/outputs/apk/release/`. Official artifacts are staged in `dist/` as `ZViewer-<version>-release.apk` and an accompanying SHA-256 checksum. The repository tracks the checksums. Download official APKs from GitHub Releases.

## Key Dependencies

Kotlin `2.1.21`, Compose BOM `2025.05.01`, `activity-compose:1.10.1`, `lifecycle:2.9.0`, `core-ktx:1.16.0`, Media3 `exoplayer` / `ui` `1.6.1`, kotlinx-coroutines `1.10.2`, `me.zhanghai.android.libarchive:library:1.1.6`, APNG4Android `apng` / `avif` `3.0.5`, `org.aomedia.avif.android:avif:1.3.0.841110fd`.
